holidays.name: Chant at the Moon Day
holidays.description: Step outside after dark, look up at the moon, and let loose with a chant, a hum, a howl or a made-up mantra. There are no rules about what you chant or how well you do it. Neighbors may be confused, but the moon won't mind.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits August's bright summer skies and the long human habit of singing to the moon.
holidays.funFact: People have honored the moon with songs and rituals for thousands of years. Many harvest and moon festivals around the world happen in late summer and early autumn.

holidays.name: National Lemon Meringue Pie Day
holidays.description: A day for the pie with a tart, sunny lemon filling under a cloud of toasted, sugary meringue. Bake one from scratch or grab a slice from your favorite diner. Either way, the sweet-and-sour combination is the point.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is one of many dessert days on the American calendar.
holidays.funFact: A weeping meringue, where beads of moisture form between the meringue and the filling, is a classic baking headache. Spreading the meringue over a hot filling helps prevent it.

holidays.name: Relaxation Day
holidays.description: This is an official excuse to do as little as possible. Put down the to-do list, silence your phone, and nap, stretch, or stare at the clouds. It lands in the middle of August, when the summer slump is in full swing.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is widely listed on August 15 as a mid-summer reminder to take a break.
holidays.funFact: Many European countries have an August holiday on this same date, so a lot of people there are already relaxing. In places like Italy, Ferragosto on August 15 kicks off a traditional holiday break.
